q: I sprayed chlorantraniliprole on my brinjal yesterday. When can I harvest?
answer: Chlorantraniliprole has a long waiting period on brinjal: 22 days. Since you sprayed on 20 October, don't pick any brinjal before 11 November 2026. Keep cutting and destroying wilted shoots in the meantime. Please confirm the product with your Agriculture Knowledge Centre.

q: I sprayed chlorantraniliprole on my brinjal yesterday. When can I harvest?
answer: Wait until 25 Kartik 2083 (11 November 2026) before harvesting. The label waiting period for chlorantraniliprole on brinjal is 22 days, counted from your last spray.

q: Is chlorpyrifos still allowed? The agrovet still sells it.
answer: No. Chlorpyrifos was banned in Nepal in December 2024. Shops are allowed to sell off old stock for up to two years, but that doesn't make it safe or recommended, so please don't use it.

q: I sprayed acetamiprid on cabbage 5 days ago, can I sell tomorrow?
answer: Not yet. Acetamiprid needs 7 days on cabbage. You sprayed on 16 October, so wait until 23 October 2026 (6 Kartik 2083 BS) before you harvest or sell.

q: chilli mites what can I use
answer: Spray the underside of the leaves, because that is where mites live. Buprofezin (5 days waiting period on chilli) and chlorfenapyr (5 days) are on the label for chilli mites. Confirm with your Agriculture Knowledge Centre.

q: I sprayed broflanilide on okra today. When can I pick?
answer: Broflanilide has a 1 day waiting period on okra, so you can pick from tomorrow, 22 October 2026.
